title: Meridian instruction source registry
description: Container for registered instruction sources. Each entry is a scoped record: its envelope (identity, scope, origin, authority) is validated separately against scoped-record.schema.json, and this schema is not a second envelope schema. This schema adds the container shape and the source-snapshot contract carried in each entry's payload. read_channel describes only who observes the SOURCE and how (the agent's own tool ingests the file, Meridian's registry reads it to snapshot it, or a person reports its state); it never describes delivery of a norm to an agent. Registering a source, and reading it to snapshot it, grant its text no authority and do not bypass controlled-rule-intake, which alone parses discovered text into rules and takes an acceptance decision. Temporal model: recorded_state is the snapshot the registry currently holds for the source; divergence.previous_state is the snapshot held before the last check; divergence.current_state is the fresh observation that check produced. recorded_state and divergence.current_state describe one and the same present observation and must not disagree on revision, digest OR verification state; previous_state is historical and may differ, except on source-missing / source-unreadable where the last-known recorded_state must equal previous_state. Two verified states are unchanged only when BOTH revision and SHA-256 digest match; a difference in either is changed. currency is one of current | stale | unverified — stale is a verified last-known state whose source has since gone missing or become unreadable (not merely changed: on a changed result the registry re-records the fresh observation, so recorded_state is current), and is never a substitute for an unverified snapshot. Registering a source grants its text no norm authority: every payload declares normative_status = not-a-norm and record_type is instruction-source, never norm. The rules JSON Schema cannot state live in scripts/lib/instruction-source-registry.mjs. The instruction-source-registry contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The normative document is standards/workspace/instruction-source-registry.md.

sha256_digest.description: A source state is fixed by a SHA-256 digest and nothing weaker. algorithm is a single accepted value; value is 64 lowercase hex characters.

observed_state.description: A previous or current observation of the source used to compute divergence. verified is whether this exact state was actually read back from the source; an unverified state cannot support an unchanged or changed claim. Two verified states are unchanged only when both revision and digest.value match.

normative_status.description: The only accepted value. Registration does not grant the source's text the authority of a norm, accept a rule or resolve a conflict.

medium.description: The declared bearer of the source. The location is confined to it: a file source is located by a relative path AND an opaque container identity; a service source by opaque service and resource identifiers with no filesystem path.

format.description: The shape of the source content. Modelled separately from the read channel: neither is derived from the other.

location.description: Where the source is, confined to the declared medium. The two forms are mutually exclusive: medium 'file' requires path + container_ref and forbids service_ref + resource_ref; medium 'external-service' requires service_ref + resource_ref and forbids path + container_ref. No absolute path, no escape through '..' and no hidden fallback resolution: missing_behavior has one accepted value, and the confinement of a relative path and the opacity of every reference are enforced in scripts/lib/instruction-source-registry.mjs.

path.description: For medium 'file' only (required there, forbidden elsewhere): a POSIX-relative path inside the declared medium. Absolute paths, a leading '/', a drive letter, a backslash separator and '.'/'..' segments are rejected by the library check.

container_ref.description: For medium 'file' only (required there, forbidden elsewhere): an opaque identifier of the repository or workspace that bears the file — the identity of the medium, never a machine path. Absolute forms and '..' segments are rejected by the library check.

service_ref.description: For medium 'external-service' only (required there, forbidden elsewhere): opaque identifier of the service.

resource_ref.description: For medium 'external-service' only (required there, forbidden elsewhere): opaque identifier of the resource within the service.

missing_behavior.description: The only accepted value. When the source cannot be resolved the registry fails closed; it does not fall back to a parent directory, a cached copy or a plausible sibling. Its absence is undeclared fallback behaviour and is rejected.

recorded_state.description: The snapshot the registry currently holds for the source: an explicit revision and a SHA-256 digest. revision_verified is whether that snapshot was read back from the source. currency states how the snapshot relates to the source now: 'current' (verified, and divergence.status is not source-missing / source-unreadable), 'stale' (verified once, but a later check found the source missing or unreadable — the last known state; NOT used for 'changed', where the fresh observation is re-recorded and the snapshot is current), 'unverified' (never verified). The library check binds currency to revision_verified and to divergence.status.

read_channel.description: Who observes the SOURCE and how, modelled separately from the format. This is not a norm-delivery channel: registering or reading a source grants its text no authority (see controlled-rule-intake). 'agent-native' — the agent's own tool ingests the source file itself (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules) and Meridian is not in that read path. 'meridian-observed' — Meridian's registry reads the source to take its snapshot. 'manual' — a person observes the source and reports its state. The agent-native channel has an explicit visibility boundary: Meridian cannot fully observe what the agent's own tool does with the source (enforced in the library check).

meridian_visibility.description: How completely Meridian's registry can observe this source on its way to an agent. 'full' is possible only on the meridian-observed channel; the agent-native channel, where the agent's own tool ingests the source, is never 'full'.

agent_auto_read.description: True when the agent's own tooling ingests this source itself, without Meridian in the read path. Ties to kind 'agent-native'.

divergence.description: The result of comparing the snapshot held before the last check (previous_state) with the fresh observation that check produced (current_state). 'unchanged' and 'changed' are computed only from two verifiable states; 'unknown' is allowed only when the evidence is genuinely insufficient — never when both states are present and verified. 'source-missing' and 'source-unreadable' carry no current_state at all: a source that cannot be observed has no current state; and when they carry a previous_state, recorded_state (the last-known state) must equal it on revision and digest. current_state, when present, describes the same present observation as recorded_state and must not disagree with it on revision, digest or verification state.
